correctness.rationale: For at least two initial blue cycle vertices, connectedness forces a unique proper cyclic interval (or the whole cycle) and forbids a blue leaf with a white parent. A single leaf can at most supply its parent, which still has two white cycle neighbors. A boundary can enter the gap exactly when its private leaf is absent or blue. Its front reaches the first decorated gap vertex, but cannot proceed beyond it while the farther cycle neighbor is white: the private leaf of the stalled vertex must also be white. If the two reach lengths leave a middle interval, a first force into it is therefore impossible, including an inactive initial boundary as a zero-length front. Otherwise the fronts cover the gap, after which parents force all unselected leaves. This includes a one-vertex gap and the triangle. Optional interior leaves have independent factors 1+z; boundary weights encode initial leaf selection exactly and proper intervals are counted once. New exhaustive subset code reproduced both n=7 coefficient vectors, 1023 nonempty subsets each. The universal statement follows from the proof, not the finite checks.
